tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a file, view an image, or list a directory. Large text files are shown as bounded excerpts with their file size; use a line range to inspect a specific section. Directory listings are non-recursive and show up to 50 entries by default.

filePath.description: File or directory path on this Node. Relative paths use the session working directory supplied for this Node, or its agent directory if unset. Absolute paths and ~/ paths are accepted subject to permissions. On master and CLI Nodes, a leading $fw_agentdir or $fw_tmp expands to this Agent's directory or its tmp directory. Other leading $ names are rejected.

startLine.description: First line to read, counting from 1. For directories, the first entry to list. Omit or use 0 to start at the beginning.

endLine.description: Last line or directory entry to include, counting from 1. Omit or use 0 for the default range.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write text to a file on this Node. Existing files are protected unless overwrite is true; missing parent directories are created only when createDirs is true.

filePath.description: Destination path on this Node. Relative paths use the session working directory supplied for this Node, or its agent directory if unset. Absolute paths and ~/ paths are accepted subject to permissions. On master and CLI Nodes, a leading $fw_agentdir or $fw_tmp expands to this Agent's directory or its tmp directory. Other leading $ names are rejected.

overwrite.description: Allow replacement of an existing file. Defaults to false.

createDirs.description: Create missing parent directories. Defaults to false.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit files using exact text replacements or a patch. For one replacement, supply filePath, oldText and newText. For multiple replacements in one file, supply filePath and edits; all entries match the original content and must not overlap. Alternatively, supply apply_patch to add, modify or delete files using patch text. Use only one form per call.

filePath.description: File to edit on this Node. Relative paths use the session working directory supplied for this Node, or its agent directory if unset. Absolute paths and ~/ paths are accepted subject to permissions. On master and CLI Nodes, a leading $fw_agentdir or $fw_tmp expands to this Agent's directory or its tmp directory. Other leading $ names are rejected.

oldText.description: Exact text to replace. Must be nonempty and match once unless replaceAll is true.

newText.description: Replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the matched text.

replaceAll.description: Replace every non-overlapping occurrence of oldText. Defaults to false.

edits.description: Replacements in one file, all matched against its original content. Entries must not overlap.

oldText.description: Exact text to replace. Must be nonempty and match once unless replaceAll is true.

newText.description: Replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the matched text.

replaceAll.description: Replace every non-overlapping occurrence of oldText. Defaults to false.

apply_patch.description: Patch text enclosed in *** Begin Patch and *** End Patch. Use *** Update File:, *** Add File: or *** Delete File: headers. Update sections use space-prefixed context, - deletions, + additions and @@ anchors. Paths follow this Node's path rules. Do not combine with filePath or replacement arguments.

tools.name: apply_patch
tools.description: Add, modify, or delete files on this Node using the apply_patch format with *** Begin Patch and *** End Patch. Relative paths in patch headers use the session working directory supplied for this Node, or its agent directory if unset. On master and CLI Nodes, a leading $fw_agentdir or $fw_tmp expands to this Agent's directory or its tmp directory. Other leading $ names are rejected.

input.description: Complete patch text with Add File, Update File, or Delete File operations.

tools.name: exec
tools.description: Run a shell command on the current Node. Output is saved in a command log and shown as a bounded preview. If the command outlasts timeout, it continues in the background and returns an execId; a later event reports completion. The timeout does not kill the command. On supported Nodes, Stop or Run queued ends the wait without killing the command, returning available output and an execId; completion is reported later. Avoid adding head or tail just to shorten the preview: that changes the captured output. If you need both a complete log and a filtered view, save the complete output separately or use tee with a filter that consumes the whole stream. For temporary files, prefer $fw_tmp ($env:fw_tmp in PowerShell) over /tmp; fw_agentdir gives the Agent directory. These environment variables are set for Agent-owned commands on master and CLI Nodes.

summary.description: Briefly describe what this command or script will do. State its purpose, not an expected result.

command.description: Shell command or pipeline to execute.

cwd.description: Working directory for this command. Relative paths use the session working directory supplied for this Node, or the Node process working directory if unset. With no cwd, execution uses that same default chain. On master and CLI Nodes, a leading $fw_agentdir or $fw_tmp expands to this Agent's directory or its tmp directory. Other leading $ names are rejected.

secretEnv.description: Environment variables to set from stored secrets, as {"VARIABLE": "secret-name"}. The command receives the values; they are not written into the command, exec records or this conversation, and command output that contains them is masked. Available on master and on Nodes that support it.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait before returning a still-running command as a background execution. Defaults to 15; values above 60 are reduced to 60 with a warning.

tools.name: get_default_cwd
tools.description: Get this Node's process working directory, used by exec when neither a command nor the session specifies one.
